# Atlas 64

> Atlas is the modular board game console: a board with lights that recognizes the pieces placed on it and transforms for each game. It is controlled from the free Atlas HUB app and developed by WOLO Labs. It's made for role-playing games (like Dungeons & Dragons), strategy (chess and Amazonas), light-and-reflex games for families or friends, and for creating and publishing your own games with Atlas Studio. Recommended age: 14 and up. Launching soon on Kickstarter; sign-up is open at https://presale.atlas-64.com/

## How it works

- **One board, many games.** You pick the game in the Atlas HUB app (Android on Google Play, iPhone on TestFlight) and the board sets itself up: the lights mark squares, paths, walls and possible moves. There's nothing to calibrate.
- **Works offline.** The board and the app talk to each other directly over Bluetooth. An internet connection is only needed to download new games, sync your profile and get updates.
- **Modular.** Each module is a complete board. Bring another one close and it connects on its own: everything is wireless, with nothing to plug in. Up to 6 can be joined to build bigger tables and maps.
- **Detects every move.** Atlas detects each move and guides the game with lighting, so players can focus on playing.

## Pieces, smart bases and Atlas Core

- Each piece screws onto a **smart base** with a unique ID.
- **Atlas Core**, an NFC module that attaches to the edge of the board, reads the base placed on it and the board says which piece it is.
- **Each game decides what each piece represents**: a knight, a bishop, a building, a role-playing character.
- **Figures are interchangeable**: unscrew one, screw on another and the base stays the same.
- **Your own miniatures**: you can design and 3D print any figure with the base's thread. The base's STL model is a free download at https://atlas-64.com/#fichas and the board recognizes those pieces like any other.
- The box includes: Atlas board, smart bases, miniatures, NFC module (Atlas Core), USB-C cable, phone stand and quick-start guide.

## Atlas Studio: create games without coding

Atlas Studio lets you create games for Atlas without knowing how to code:

1. **Imagine**: tell an AI assistant your idea.
2. **Create**: Atlas Studio turns it into a game.
3. **Test**: play it on a simulated board or on your phone.
4. **Publish**: upload it to the Atlas HUB store.
5. **Share**: other players download it or buy it.

The Atlas HUB store is open to independent creators, who can publish their games for free or for sale. More information: https://atlas-64.com/ecosystem/#creadores. Creator guides: https://wololabs.com/guides.html

## Who Atlas is for

- **Role-players (Dungeons & Dragons and similar).** With **Role Mapper**, the game master creates their own maps, brings them to the board and runs the session live from the phone, triggering events and special effects. It has a camera mode to explore the whole map as if it were a video game. With expansion modules (up to 6) the world grows and can be designed however you like, and thanks to the interchangeable pieces each player can design and use their own miniature: Atlas recognizes it. With Atlas Studio you can also create your own adventures and games.
- **Chess and strategy players.** **Chess** comes with the Stockfish engine, with 10 difficulty levels from beginner to grandmaster, move analysis and games against another person with an adjustable clock. **Amazonas** is an Argentine abstract strategy game, with an AI at three levels.
- **Families and groups of friends who want to play together at the table, away from screens.** The game happens on the board, with physical pieces and lights; the phone is only used as a controller. For two: **Maze** (easy, 5 to 15 minutes). With lights and reflexes: **PONGol** (table soccer played with light) and **La Luz Mala** (puzzles). For groups of 3 to 6: **Estación Lunar** and **Plagio en la Academia** (hidden roles and deduction). Recommended for ages 14 and up; not suitable for children under 3 because of small parts.
- **Game creators and designers.** Atlas Studio turns an idea into a game without coding, and the Atlas HUB store lets you publish and sell it.
- **3D printing and miniature painting fans.** Any figure with the base's thread becomes a piece the board recognizes.

## Games

### Role Mapper

Tool for role-playing games · tool, no fixed number of players · Open-ended · difficulty varies · https://atlas-64.com/games/role-mapper/

A tool for creating role-playing game maps on the Atlas 64 board. Create maps, edit them and run the session live.

Features:
- Map creation
- Live session control
- Custom events and special effects

### Chess

Powered by Stockfish · 1 to 2 players · 10–60 min · difficulty varies · https://atlas-64.com/games/ajedrez/

Challenge the AI or face a friend in the classic strategy game. With the built-in Stockfish engine, the AI adapts to your level, from beginner to grandmaster.

Features:
- Built-in Stockfish engine
- 10 difficulty levels
- Player vs. AI and Player vs. Player
- Move analysis

How to play:
1. Move the pieces following the standard rules of chess.
2. The goal is to checkmate your opponent's king.
3. In Player vs. Player mode you can set the clock.

### Maze

The labyrinth of the shattered god · 2 players · 5–15 min · difficulty easy · https://atlas-64.com/games/maze/

Ages ago, an ancient god sealed away his treasure so it would never fall into unworthy hands. He didn't hide it in chests or vaults, but in a living labyrinth where the walls can't be seen and the path shifts at the god's will. The treasure was split into five sacred fragments. Only whoever gathers them all can claim the god's favor.

Features:
- Punishes those who move carelessly
- Rewrites its corridors when disturbed
- Multiple labyrinths

How to play:
1. Each player starts in a corner of the labyrinth.
2. Collect the 5 treasure fragments to win.
3. Avoid the walls or you go back to the start.
4. Gather special powers that help you in your search.

### Amazonas

Created by Walter Zamkauskas · 1 to 2 players · 10–30 min · difficulty varies · https://atlas-64.com/games/amazonas/

Pure abstract strategy, invented by Argentine designer Walter Zamkauskas in 1988 and adapted to the Atlas 64 board. Each player commands four Amazons that move like a chess queen and, after every move, shoot an arrow that blocks a square for good. The territory shrinks turn by turn and whoever runs out of moves loses: draws are impossible.

Features:
- Player vs. player
- Against the AI at three levels: Beginner, Intermediate and Expert
- AI powered by Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS)
- 8×8 board, adapted from the original 10×10
- The game ends on its own once the territories are sealed off

How to play:
1. Each player has 4 Amazons. White moves first, then players take turns.
2. Each turn has two mandatory, inseparable parts: move an Amazon and shoot an arrow.
3. Amazons move like a chess queen: in a straight or diagonal line, any number of empty squares, without jumping over Amazons or arrows.
4. After moving, the Amazon shoots an arrow from her new position with the same reach as a queen. The square where it lands stays blocked for the rest of the game.
5. The first player who can't move and shoot on their turn loses. There are no draws: the last player to move wins.
6. If the territories are sealed off and no contested areas remain, the game ends on its own and whoever has more available squares wins.

### La Luz Mala

Created by Luis Olcese · 1 to 4 players · 10–20 min · difficulty medium · https://atlas-64.com/games/la-luz-mala/

Those who follow it never return. Those who know, guide it. A logic puzzle game: place the objects on the board so the light reaches every den.

Features:
- Logic puzzles
- Procedurally generated levels

How to play:
1. Place the objects before the light passes.
2. Make the light reach every den.
3. If it hits a tree or leaves the board, it's lost.

### PONGol

Created by Luis Olcese · 1 to 4 players · 5–15 min · difficulty medium · https://atlas-64.com/games/pongol/

Table soccer played with light. The ball is a yellow light that never stops moving across the 8×8 pitch. You don't control a player: you place real pieces on the board to build walls and deflect the ball toward the opposing goal. With an electronic referee, VAR and cards: lift a piece too soon or step into your rival's half and you'll pay for it.

Features:
- Against the AI or 1 vs 1 at the same table
- Four ball speeds: Slow, Normal, Fast and Flash
- Electronic referee with VAR and yellow and red cards
- Academy: a 5-lesson tutorial to master the bounces
- Played by placing physical pieces on the board

How to play:
1. The goal is to get the yellow light into your rival's goal. The goals are the first and last rows of the board, lit in white.
2. Each team has 2 pieces and can only place them in its own half of the pitch.
3. 3-second rule: when you place a piece, its LED turns orange and the piece is locked. Only once it turns blue can you lift it.
4. Bounces: head-on, the ball comes back the way it came; if it hits the front of a piece diagonally, it straightens out; a corner graze deflects it without slowing it down; a hit right on the tip sends it back where it came from; and two pieces with a gap between them form a corridor the ball goes straight through.
5. Yellow card: lifting a piece before its LED turns blue, invading your rival's half or placing more pieces than allowed. Every offense goes to VAR first.
6. Red card: the same team's second yellow. The rest of the play is played with a single piece.
7. If a team gets a second red card, the rival is awarded a goal by default.
8. Amnesty: every goal scored clears all cards and gives both teams their two pieces back.
9. Before kickoff, a pulsing purple light shows where the ball will shoot off. It goes out when play starts.
10. First to 5 goals wins.

### Estación Lunar

Deception and hidden roles · 3 to 4 players · 20–50 min · difficulty medium · https://atlas-64.com/games/estacion-lunar/

We are scientists in a lunar colony. On a routine patrol we found someone unconscious and, ever since they joined us, strange things have been happening… An alien creature has infiltrated the colony, and there may also be a Saboteur from another colony.

Features:
- Three 8×8 maps: Zone Alpha, Delta Corridor and Gamma Core
- The Stranger, run by the app, fills the table when there's an odd number of players
- LEDs mark walls, machines, vents and the squares you can reach
- Skill mini-game to repair the machines
- Meetings with secret ballots
- Step-by-step guided tutorial

Roles:
- **Scientists**: kill the Creature with a Reagent, made by collecting 6 Components scattered across the board.
- **Creature**: infect every other player, or hold out until the rounds run out.
- **Saboteur**: sabotage the colony until all its machines are broken.

How to play:
1. Each player sees their role in secret on the phone. With an odd number of players, the Stranger joins in: a character that plays on its own.
2. On their turn, each player moves as many squares as their Sanity allows.
3. Passing over a Component picks it up. With 6 you get a Reagent.
4. Machines break down by chance or through sabotage. Repairing one takes two players standing next to it.
5. Once per turn, anyone can call a Meeting to vote on who the Saboteur is or whom to inject with the Reagent.
6. Every 2 rounds, a report reveals how many crew members are infected, and Sanity drops.
7. The game includes an interactive tutorial that explains everything step by step, and you can replay it from the menu.

### Plagio en la Academia

Social deduction · 3 to 6 players · 15–30 min · difficulty medium · https://atlas-64.com/games/plagio-en-la-academia/

Welcome to the Royal Academy of Visual Arts. The Rector has uncovered a scandal: among the new students are impostors who faked their portfolios. To protect the institution's reputation, he has set a surprise exam: reproduce a secret mosaic. The true artists know the plan; the impostors must improvise every brushstroke to avoid being expelled.

Features:
- Hidden roles: Prodigies vs. Frauds
- Shared 8×8 canvas and pigment palette
- Accusations and votes at any time
- Limit of 50 brushstrokes per game

How to play:
1. Secret roles depend on the number of students: with 3 or 4 players there is 1 Fraud; with 5 or 6 there are 2. Everyone else is a Prodigy, a real artist.
2. Portfolio inspection: taking turns in secret, each student taps the screen to see their role. Prodigies see the 8×8 Secret Mosaic; Frauds only see a warning, with no plan or guide.
3. The exam is played in turns on a shared 8×8 canvas. On your turn, pick a color from the palette and paint a square.
4. If you're a Prodigy, place the exact color at the right coordinate according to your plan.
5. If you're a Fraud, blend in: watch where the others paint and copy the pattern so nobody suspects you.
6. Formal accusation: at any time a student can call the Rector. Painting stops and everyone votes on the suspect.
7. The Prodigies win if they expel every Fraud. The Frauds win if an innocent Prodigy is accused.
8. Stroke limit: if the canvas reaches 50 brushstrokes without a successful accusation, the exam ends and the Frauds win.

### Pixel Blaster

Arcade · 1 player · 5–15 min · difficulty medium · https://atlas-64.com/games/pixel-blaster/

Seven four-block pieces fall nonstop into the well, and your only job is to keep it from filling up. Rotate them, slide them and slam them down to complete full rows of eight blocks. The more you clear, the faster they fall. You don't win this game: you survive it.

Features:
- 7 different pieces, each with its own color
- 8×16 well with two modules, or 8×8 with just one
- Ghost piece and next-piece preview
- Hard drop and rotate from the controller pad
- Progressive levels and session high score

How to play:
1. Pieces fall one at a time from the top of the well. Move them left and right, rotate them and drop them before they hit the bottom.
2. The well is 8 columns by 16 rows when two modules are connected. With a single module it shrinks to 8×8 so the whole game fits on the board.
3. Complete a full row of 8 blocks and it bursts: everything above it drops down one square.
4. One row scores 100 points, two score 300, three score 500 and four at once score 800. The total is multiplied by your current level.
5. Every 10 rows cleared you go up a level and the pieces start falling faster.
6. The faint ghost below the piece shows where it will land, and the Next indicator shows which piece comes after.
7. Hard drop slams the piece instantly into the ghost's position.
8. The game ends when a new piece comes in and there's no room left for it.
